Shorten the fully resolved gradient from injection 1 while retaining its low starting organic fraction to separate the early peaks. Changing only tG tests slope sensitivity of the critical late pair and should bring the last peak close to or below 10 minutes.

Injection 9 reached the maximum CRF with substantial resolution margin. Shortening tG to 8 minutes tests a faster fully resolved method while keeping injection 9 as the established optimum-score fallback.
Reduce tG by one grid step to shorten the separation while testing whether the early pair retains R ≥ 1.5. Injection 10 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains a fully resolved fallback.

Test the next shorter gradient to locate the fastest fully resolved method at 45 C. The early pair is approaching the resolution threshold, so this run will establish whether 4 minutes is viable or 6 minutes is needed.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to recover the early pair’s small resolution deficit while retaining the 4-minute gradient. The last peak previously eluted near 0.82 organic fraction, so a 0.90 endpoint should still keep all peaks within the gradient.

Raise temperature by one grid step to test whether the run can be shortened while preserving full resolution. Keeping the gradient unchanged isolates temperature’s effect on the critical early pair, whose current R is only 1.54.

The temperature increase worsened early-pair selectivity, so test 40 C to recover resolution with the steeper 0.95-endpoint gradient. This could retain CRF 1.000 while eluting the last peak slightly sooner than injection 13.

Test a 2-minute gradient, using lower temperature and a narrower solvent window to offset compression of the critical early pair. The high endpoint should permit rapid elution of the last compound during the final hold, potentially improving on injection 15’s separation time while preserving maximum CRF.

Reduce the endpoint by one grid step to make the gradient slightly shallower and recover the early pair’s tiny resolution deficit. The last peak will elute later during the hold, but should remain comfortably below 10 minutes.

Shift the 2-minute gradient window upward while preserving injection 17’s slope, aiming to shorten the late peak’s hold-phase retention. This tests whether the early pair remains fully resolved at a moderately higher starting organic fraction.

Shift the window upward another grid step at the same slope to shorten the last peak’s hold-phase retention. Injection 18 preserved early-pair resolution, so test whether this further shift also retains the maximum CRF.

Shift both endpoints upward one more grid step while maintaining the slope that preserved full resolution in injections 17–19. This should shorten the last peak’s retention further, while testing whether the early pair remains sufficiently retained and resolved.

Raise the starting organic fraction one grid step to test further shortening at the minimum gradient duration. The shallower slope may help resolution, but the early pair’s proximity to the dead time makes this a useful boundary test; injection 20 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one grid step to shorten retention while using the early pair’s resolution margin of 1.77. Keeping the gradient fixed tests whether this modest temperature increase preserves full resolution at the minimum gradient duration.

Test a higher starting organic fraction, returning to 25 C to favor early-pair selectivity as those peaks approach the dead time. This probes the upper starting-solvent boundary; injection 22 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to the starting fraction that retained the early pair and slightly reduce gradient steepness to increase its resolution margin. This tests a more robust maximum-score alternative to injection 22, accepting a modest increase in the last peak’s retention.

Use the final injection to test a short, maximum-score candidate with greater early-pair resolution margin: lower temperature favors selectivity, and the slightly shallower gradient should improve separation relative to injection 20. Injection 22 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
